newsitem.title: USA: U.S. supports Plavsic in Bosnian Serb court case.
newsitem.headline: U.S. supports Plavsic in Bosnian Serb court case.

text.p: The United States on Friday said Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic acted within her powers when she dissolved parliament and condemned what it said were efforts to intimidate the Bosnian Serb court into ruling against her.

"Our analysis and international analysis has determined that ... Mrs. Plavsic was fully within her powers in dissolving the assembly and that the current challenges to her actions are not legally valid," State Department spokesman James Rubin told reporters.
Moments after Rubin spoke, the Bosnian Serb Constitutional Court ruled against Plavsic's decision last month to disband the Serb parliament and call early elections.

U.S. envoy Robert Gelbard is to leave for Bosnia on Sunday with a multipurpose agenda that includes trying to prevent Bosnian Serb leaders from trying to politicize legal actions against Plavsic, Rubin said.
The spokesman said Bosnian Serb court justices were "under intense political pressure to decide this case. And we are aware of specific acts of intimidation."
"We regard these acts as fundamentally wrong in that they are trying to flout the rule of law there that we are working so hard to create," he said.

"The bottom line is that there is a struggle going on in the Republika Srpska between those who are smart enough to realize that compliance with Dayton (peace accords) is the ticket to prosperity and peace for their people, and those leaders who are too stupid to realize that a failure to comply with Dayton, a failure to follow through on the international community's demands will only make their people suffer," he said.
